The eccentric exercise resulted in a significant 62% increase in IGF-1 mRNA concentrations as opposed to a nonsignificant increase from concentric exercise. In addition, eccentric exercise caused a reduction of IGFBP-4 mRNA-a strong inhibitor of IGF-1-by 57%, whereas the concentric condition showed only modest changes in the levels of this protein. Importantly, results were positively correlated with markers of muscle damage, suggesting that the IGF-1 system is involved in the repair process.
